if it is rusting, it is steel. Almost all metals react to oxygen in one way or another and corrode. And steel is special enough to get it's own name for that corrosion, wich is rust.

I might be using wrong terms here so maybe @Rotteuxx can chime in as well.
for steel and oxygen to react it needs a catalyst, and most common catalyst is water. so if you have a pice of steel inside it will stop rusting further as long as humidity (water in air) is low. What i have done in the past with great success is just get the los rust of with a wire brush and then just use rust paint (like tremclad) and cover it all. indoors it will last for years. outside if it comes into contact with to much moisture the rust might start eating through the paint from the inside. Rust on steel is like cancer, once it's there it will be there and spread unless you remove it completely. Rust paint will slow down the spread significantly.

A rust inhibitor prior to painting could help if for outdoor use. Key is cleaning and using primer to ensure a good chemical bond... & a decent thickness of paint to make sure it's sealed & wear resistant.
